**Visual Analysis:**
- **Affected part**: Wheat leaves (multiple plants)
- **Key features**: 
  - Numerous small, round, white/cream-colored spots scattered across leaf surfaces
  - Spots appear powdery/mottled in texture
  - Some leaves show orange/tan discoloration (possible necrosis or co-infection)
  - Spots are randomly distributed, not in stripes or rows
  - Stems appear healthy/green

**Differential reasoning:**
- **Powdery Mildew**: White powdery spots/colonies on leaf surfaces — strong match with the white spots
- **Wheat Leaf Rust**: Orange-brown pustules randomly scattered — color doesn't match (these are white, not orange)
- **Stripe Rust**: Yellow pustules in linear stripes along leaf veins — pattern doesn't match
- **Septoria Leaf Blotch**: Brown irregular blotches — doesn't match
- **Tan Spot**: Tan oval lesions with dark borders — doesn't match

The white/cream powdery-looking scattered spots on the leaves are characteristic of **Powdery Mildew** (*Blumeria graminis*), which produces white powdery colonies on wheat leaves.
